subject: possible to model piecewise growth modeling using lavaan?

messages.subject: possible to model piecewise growth modeling using lavaan?
parts:
Dear lavaan community,

I'm taking baby steps with learning how to conduct piecewise growth modeling and I wonder if this can be done using lavaan? I've read through a lavaan tutorial on latent growth curves  but I can't even begin how to imagine how to modify it to address my research questions. 

Here is a brief summary of my data and my research questions:

I have about 300 students that are clustered in 48 classrooms or teachers that come from 4 school districts and their reading and mathematics achievement is tracked across 3 years.  Each student was tested 3 times (fall, winter, and spring) within each year, so they all have 9 data points across 3 years.  However, the testing times vary across students and schools, i.e., time-varying observations.  Plotting the individual growth curves shows that within each year, students' performance increases in a linear fashion, but there is a slight dip in performance at the beginning of year 2 compared to at the end of year 1, and at the beginning of year 3 compared to at the end of year 2.  Hence, I believe I should model their growth with 3 intercept growth factors and 3 slope growth factors. After that, I'm hoping to enter teacher level predictors hoping to account for some of the variation in students' growth.  

If you have a piecewise growth model syntax sample out there that you're willing to share, that would be really great but any guidance would be wonderful.  Also, after having examined some examples in papers and in forums, I'm still scratching my head about how to specify time scores because I've seen people specify them very differently, but there's very little explanation of why they specified them that way.  In my example, I'm guessing that it's like this.  Could someone please confirm whether I'm on the right track? 
0 1 2                        (time scores piece 1)
         0 1 2               (time scores piece 2)
                  0 1 2       (time scores piece 3)


0 1 2 because I'm assuming that the growth is linear.  However, do these time scores assume that there's equal spacing between time 1, time 2, and time 3? If so, my data won't meet this assumption because students get tested at different times within a single testing period (i.e., fall, winter, spring). 


Thank you for your kind attention on this and for any input you can provide.
